title: Google Sheets ARRAYFORMULA
description: Google Sheets ARRAYFORMULA applies one formula to an entire range at once, so you never copy down again. Learn how to combine it with IF, FILTER, and QUERY.
intro: Copying a formula down hundreds of rows is tedious and brittle — insert a row and the pattern breaks. Google Sheets' ARRAYFORMULA solves this by applying a single formula to a whole range and spilling the results automatically. This guide covers the core pattern and how to combine it with IF, FILTER, and QUERY.
prerequisites: A Google Sheets spreadsheet to test in
Awareness that ARRAYFORMULA is Google Sheets only

sections.title: What ARRAYFORMULA Does
sections.content: ARRAYFORMULA wraps any formula and evaluates it for every cell in the input range at once, returning a spilled array of results. Instead of writing =A2*B2 in C2 and dragging down, you reference the full columns and let Sheets calculate each row in a single cell.

example.result: A column of products, one per row of A2:A10 and B2:B10
example.explanation: The multiplication is applied element-by-element. Place the formula in one cell (e.g. C2) and it fills C2:C10 automatically.

tips: Leave the cells below the formula empty so the array has room to spill.

sections.title: Replacing Fill-Down with One Formula
sections.content: The most common use is to replace a column of copied formulas with a single spilling formula. Write the formula you would copy down, then swap the single-cell references for full column ranges and wrap everything in ARRAYFORMULA.

steps.name: Use full ranges
steps.text: Change references to the whole column range.

steps.name: Wrap with ARRAYFORMULA
steps.text: Enclose the expression so Sheets spills it.

tips: This pattern survives inserted rows because the range reference expands with the data.

sections.title: Combining ARRAYFORMULA with IF
sections.content: IF normally returns one value, but inside ARRAYFORMULA it is applied to every row. This is perfect for row-by-row conditional calculations such as tiered commissions or status flags.

example.result: 10% commission for each row above 1000, else 0
example.explanation: The condition A2:A100 > 1000 is evaluated per row, and the true/false branches are computed element-by-element.

tips: Avoid aggregators like SUM inside ARRAYFORMULA — they collapse to one value; use row-by-row math or SUMPRODUCT instead.

sections.title: ARRAYFORMULA with FILTER and QUERY
sections.content: ARRAYFORMULA pairs naturally with other array functions. You can transform a FILTER result in place, or pre-compute a column that QUERY then references. These combinations let you build entire report tables from one cell.

example.result: Rows where B > 50, with numeric columns increased by 10%
example.explanation: FILTER returns the qualifying rows, and ARRAYFORMULA applies the 10% increase to the numeric values before spilling.

tips: For very large datasets, QUERY or a pivot table can be faster than one giant ARRAYFORMULA.

sections.title: Excel Equivalent: Dynamic Arrays
sections.content: ARRAYFORMULA is a Google Sheets exclusive. In Excel 365, the same effect comes from implicit dynamic arrays — =A2:A10*B2:B10 spills on its own with no wrapper. In older Excel you would need Ctrl+Shift+Enter to force array evaluation, which is exactly what ARRAYFORMULA does in Sheets.

example.result: Spills automatically in Excel 365; requires Ctrl+Shift+Enter in legacy Excel
example.explanation: Excel 365 recognizes an array expression and spills it, so ARRAYFORMULA is unnecessary there.

tips: If a spilled array lands on occupied cells in Sheets, you get #REF! — clear the target range first.

functionsUsed.name: ARRAYFORMULA
functionsUsed.description: ARRAYFORMULA lets you apply a single formula to an entire range of cells automatically, expanding results into neighboring rows and columns without manually filling down or across.

functionsUsed.name: QUERY
functionsUsed.description: QUERY runs a Google Visualization API Query Language statement on a range of data. It's Google Sheets' most powerful data function — essentially SQL for your spreadsheet.

functionsUsed.name: FILTER
functionsUsed.description: FILTER extracts rows from a range that meet a condition, returning a dynamic array of matching results. It's the array-era replacement for complex IF/INDEX combinations.

functionsUsed.name: SEQUENCE
functionsUsed.description: SEQUENCE returns a dynamic array of sequential numbers, shaped by the number of rows and columns, starting at a given value and stepping by a given increment.

summary: Google Sheets ARRAYFORMULA lets one formula replace an entire column of copied-down calculations by evaluating a range element-by-element and spilling the results. Combine it with IF for row-wise conditions, with FILTER or QUERY for in-formula data shaping, and remember there is no Excel equivalent — Excel 365 uses implicit dynamic arrays instead. Keep the spill range clear to avoid #REF! errors.
